decisions.reason: This award-backed yogurt fits the core organic dairy range well, and if it is still selling in 2022 management would usually keep it unless assortment simplification becomes necessary.
As a once-prominent focus cheese that builds directly on the firm's established cheese competence, it remains strategically suitable and is unlikely to be withdrawn soon.

The semi-hard cheese wheel is a conventional extension of the core assortment, but its relatively standard profile makes it somewhat more exposed to later portfolio pruning than the stronger signature items.

A spicy cheese line broadens shelf appeal within the firm's cheese business, though multiple variants raise the chance that weaker models or the line itself could be streamlined if turnover is only average.
This mild creamy soft cheese appears to play a clear assortment-completing role and therefore still deserves a place in the portfolio absent clear signs of underperformance.

The washed-rind soft cheese is the most niche and potentially hardest-to-scale item in a narrow organic dairy range, so management would be comparatively likely to discontinue it and redeploy resources.
